title: Top-tier Ranked Delegates must police their peers' vote explanations as a condition of being paid
content:
A.1.6.4.5 assigns an enforcement function to the highest-paid delegates: "Level 1 and Level 2 Ranked Delegates are responsible for monitoring Aligned Delegate compliance with communication responsibilities... **as a condition of their compensated position**."

The procedure is deliberately structured to reduce social cost and to break up coordination. Reports go "via private communication to the Core Facilitator," never publicly. When one RD flags a possible non-compliance, "the Core Facilitator may prompt all Level 1 and Level 2 Ranked Delegates to submit individual assessments via private communication," and "each Ranked Delegate must submit their assessment when prompted." Crucially, the facilitator "may also select specific vote explanations and prompt all Level 1 and Level 2 Ranked Delegates to submit compliance assessments, regardless of whether a Ranked Delegate has independently flagged the explanation." Failure to submit when prompted is itself a Tier 1 breach.

Several things are solved at once. **Capacity**: assessing whether every explanation demonstrates understanding of a proposal's mechanisms is expert work at volume, and the Core Facilitator cannot do it alone. **Independence**: individual private assessments prevent delegates from converging on a shared answer, so the facilitator receives genuinely separate judgments. **Cover**: because the facilitator can initiate a review of any explanation unprompted, a delegate whose work is examined cannot infer that a peer reported them — which is what makes it possible to police colleagues one must otherwise work alongside.

Mandatory response is what stops the system degrading into mutual forbearance. A voluntary scheme among a handful of well-paid peers, all subject to the same standards, has an obvious equilibrium: nobody flags anybody. Making non-submission a procedural breach removes silence as an option.

The deeper point is that top-rank compensation buys governance *labour*, not just voting. It also concentrates responsibility where the least incentive exists to challenge the system — appointed delegates (A.1.6.4.1.1.3) reviewing formula-ranked ones.
description: A.1.6.4.5 makes monitoring by Level 1 and 2 RDs a compensated duty, with private reporting to the Core Facilitator and a Tier 1 breach for failing to assess when prompted.
